# Git evidence and containment recipes on a swept tree

> **The RULE lives in CLAUDE.md; the RECIPES live here.** CLAUDE.md states that `git blame` and
> a commit SUBJECT are not evidence, that containment is a CONTENT question and never a date one,
> and that a submodule path needs its own check. This page is the command-level detail behind
> each of those, plus the exact false reading each recipe prevents.
>
> Why the split: the rule is what makes you STOP; the recipe is what you look up while executing.
> Carrying both in every agent's launch prose costs the whole fleet ~6KB per session forever
> (plan `agent-launch-context-cost-2026-09-18`, P-005).

## Why blame and subjects lie here

git-sync sweeps the WHOLE tree on a schedule, commits it under ONE identity, and labels it with
whatever agent/plan context happened to be current. So blame names the wrong person, and the
subject describes the sweeping agent's INTENT, not the diff. Both are false-positive generators,
not dead ends. A commit's `Co-Authored-By` trailer belongs in the same bucket.

For authorship, use the commissioning work-item/plan-item or a timestamp-correlated
`sessions:search`; if neither resolves, say "not attributable" — never name a person.

## Which commit carries your change

```bash
TZ=UTC git log -1 --date=iso-strict-local --format='%cd %H %s' -- <path>
```

**NOT `git rev-parse HEAD`:** the tip is routinely a DIFFERENT commit from the same sweep, so
quoting it attributes your work to a stranger's diff.

⚠ **`TZ=UTC` is INERT on `%cI`/`%aI`/`%cd`/`%ad`.** Git renders those in the COMMIT'S OWN
recorded offset — not yours, and not UTC (they all read `-0400` here only because the commits
were made on this box). Only a `--date=*-local` format honours `TZ`, which is what makes the
stamp above `+00:00` and directly comparable to Papercusp's UTC timestamps. Keep `TZ=UTC` for
`--since`/`--until` too. Misreading a `-04:00` stamp as UTC is a silent 4h skew, and it lands
exactly where it hurts — gate triage, deciding whether a fix predates a candidate.

⛔ `git log --full-history` is NOT a repair for any of this (measured identical to the default here).

Whether a sha really carries your change is a CONTENT question, never a date one:

```bash
git rev-parse <sha>:<path>      # equal blobs => it carries it
git rev-parse staging:<path>
git show --stat <sha>
```

## `HEAD` is a MOVING baseline — never read it as "before my change"

git-sync commits the WHOLE tree every few minutes, so the distance from your edit to `HEAD` is
WALL-CLOCK, not commit-count. `git show HEAD:<path>` a few minutes after an edit hands back YOUR
OWN edit, so the "pre-fix" content you test against IS your fix.

Measured 2026-08-03: a guard checked that way returned 0 offenders and read exactly like "this
guard is vacuous" — and a SOUND guard produces that identical reading, so the error is not
self-announcing in either direction. It is the clean-`git status` trap from the other side: there
a clean tree means the sweep RAN; here an ordinary-looking `HEAD` means the same thing.

Need pre-edit content? PIN the sha BEFORE you edit, or select the last commit that does NOT
contain your change BY CONTENT — never by position:

```bash
B=$(git rev-parse HEAD)                    # pin before editing
git log --oneline -n 10 -- <path>          # then: git show <sha>:<path>
scripts/mutation-probe.sh --against-last-without <literal>   # automates the selection
```

## Ancestry containment is NOT content containment

`git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-sha> <candidate>` proves only that the commit is REACHABLE
from the candidate. It stays true forever even when a later git-sync sweep overwrites or reverts
the same lines. **Never cite ancestry alone as evidence that a fix is live.**

Ask the content question against the actual candidate:

```
dev:pipeline_position { path }
state:read { cell: 'gate.greenCheckpoint.candidate', as: '<path>' }
```

Then inspect `git show <candidate>:<path>`, or compare its blob with the known-good content.
Whole-blob equality is sufficient; after legitimate later edits, verify the fix's specific
content predicate instead.

## `--verify --quiet`, and never `staging:` inside a submodule

Both misreport SILENTLY.

A bare `git rev-parse staging:<missing-path>` PRINTS the ref string to STDOUT before exiting 128,
so `S=$(git rev-parse "staging:$p" 2>/dev/null || echo ABSENT)` captures `staging:<path>` as if it
were a sha. And a SUBMODULE has no `staging` ref at all (`libs/papercusp` tracks `main`), so the
check reports a file committed minutes ago as missing — the false-NEGATIVE direction, which sends
you to re-fire git-sync or escalate "my work did not land".

```bash
# superproject
git rev-parse --verify --quiet "staging:$p" || echo ABSENT
# under a submodule
git -C libs/papercusp rev-parse --verify --quiet "HEAD:$p" || echo ABSENT
```

An unresolvable REF and an absent PATH look identical — tell them apart before acting.

## The zero-byte positive-control trap

⛔ `git show <ref>:<submodule path> > file` leaves a ZERO-BYTE file behind, so a POSITIVE CONTROL
built from it reports 0.

The shell creates the redirect BEFORE git runs, so the `fatal: path '…' exists on disk, but not
in 'HEAD'` (exit 128) still leaves an empty file, and every later `grep -c` on it returns 0 — the
exact reading that means "the string is already gone / my pattern is wrong". It defeats the one
check meant to catch a broken instrument: the control that MUST come back non-zero comes back
zero, and the whole scan is then believed.

Same false-zero family as a `| head` SIGPIPE truncation or a wrong-relation SQL zero-row. Extract
INSIDE the submodule with a SUBMODULE-relative path, and check the exit status:

```bash
git -C libs/papercusp show "HEAD:plugins/design-phase/index.cjs" > /tmp/before.cjs \
  || { echo EXTRACT-FAILED; exit 1; }
```

## Equal blobs prove that PATH is current — NOT that the candidate is

When a failing test's runtime SUBJECT lives in a submodule (e.g.
`readdirSync('…/libs/papercusp/libs/db/sql')`), the test blob is identical in both refs while the
gitlink moved underneath it — so containment answers "not stale" on a red that is pure staleness.

Diff the gitlinks too:

```bash
git diff --raw <sha> staging | grep '^:160000'
```

Measured 2026-08-30: 0 gitlinks moved at 1h, 3 at 3h, 8 at 8h — selective enough to be worth the
one command.

⛔ And `git diff <sha> staging -- <sub>/<file>` prints NOTHING for a submodule-backed path — a
superproject diff carries only the gitlink — so the empty result reads as "the subject did not
change" and CONFIRMS the wrong conclusion.

## Live/deployed status

Use `dev:pipeline_position { path }`, whose timestamps are UTC. See also
[reading pipeline state](/internal/docs/agent-insights/reading-pipeline-state-position-health-nextaction).
